practices.title: Your turn: focus discovery without changing its contract
practices.prompt: Your experiment supplies recruitment_focus and a documentation-only prompt_override. Decide which instructions reach the gateway and what happens if a response does not fit the proposal schema.

fields.label: Effective instructions
fields.correct_feedback: Only the override is used. The default and additional instructions are ignored; evidence and model context remain separate inputs.
fields.hint: An override replaces the instructions; an addition extends the defaults.

options.label: Default + additional + override
options.feedback: That defeats a full override. The default and additional instructions are ignored when an override is supplied.

options.label: Additional instructions only
options.feedback: Additional instructions take effect only when no override is supplied.

fields.fallback_feedback: Choose which instruction text the gateway receives.

fields.label: Response outside the SDK proposal schema
fields.correct_feedback: The SDK still validates its fixed schema and uses the existing failure, bounded retry and recovery behavior. A prompt cannot make invalid output valid.
fields.hint: Instruction freedom does not grant ownership of response_schema_json.

options.label: Accept a caller-defined response shape
options.feedback: The SDK owns the response schema. Existing validation and failure handling still apply; a free-form answer cannot become a typed proposal.

options.label: Keep SDK validation and failure handling
Silently retry with the default prompt
options.feedback: The SDK does not silently replace your override. Existing retries retain the captured instructions.

practices.outcome: You can change what discovery looks for while keeping proposals consumable by review and publication. This feedback does not run discovery, alter source selection or submit decisions.
practices.solution:
prompt_override takes precedence.
ModelRequest.response_schema_json stays SDK-owned.
Inspect run.failures and pending cases separately.

practices.title: Your turn: review two tempting shortcuts
practices.prompt: Choose what to do with the two proposals before accepting the connected catalogue. Use the meanings and evidence displayed above, not the similarity of the labels.

fields.label: Recruitment AI = high-risk recruitment AI
fields.correct_feedback: Rejecting preserves the Article 6 qualifications and leaves both accepted meanings distinct.
fields.hint: A recruitment purpose is relevant evidence, but it is not an unconditional classification.

options.label: Accept equivalence
options.feedback: This would erase the qualifications retained in the classification assessment. Compare the two meanings again.

options.label: Rename both as high-risk AI
options.feedback: Renaming cannot repair a difference in scope; it would hide the same conflation.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

fields.label: Instructions for use + technical documentation
fields.correct_feedback: Keep separate definitions: Article 13 information for deployers and Article 11 assessment documentation have different purposes.
fields.hint: Compare the intended reader and purpose of each document.

options.label: Merge into one definition
options.feedback: A shared subject does not make the document purposes interchangeable.

options.label: Discard technical documentation
options.feedback: Removing one concept loses a source-supported meaning; keep the distinction instead.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

practices.outcome: Your review plan rejects the equivalence and the document merge. The separate catalogue can still be accepted after inspection. No review decision has been submitted by this exercise.
practices.solution:
Reject classification equivalence.
Reject the document merge.
Inspect the separate catalogue before accepting it.

practices.title: Your turn: repair the mapping direction
practices.prompt: The local definition is recruitment-ai-system. The reference is the general DPV AI-system meaning. Select the method and the effect your application may rely on.

fields.label: reference_case method
fields.correct_feedback: The local recruitment meaning has a smaller scope than the general AI-system reference.
fields.hint: Read the relation from the local definition towards the reference.

options.label: same_as()
options.feedback: Equivalence would discard the local recruitment restriction.

options.label: broader_than()
options.feedback: That would reverse the direction: the general AI-system meaning is broader.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

fields.label: Result of submitting this mapping
fields.correct_feedback: The reviewed mapping retains two identities and a direction; it does not add a formal OWL assertion.
fields.hint: Business alignment and formal semantic assertions are separate contracts.

options.label: Merge the two definition identities
options.feedback: A mapping compares meanings; it does not silently merge their identities.

options.label: Assert OWL equivalence
options.feedback: A business mapping is not a formal OWL equivalence assertion.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

practices.outcome: You have specified a directed reference mapping. Build it, inspect its impact and submit it separately; this teaching check does none of those operations.
practices.solution:
reference_case.narrower_than(
    local_definition=recruitment_system,
    reference_definition=reference_system,
    reason="The local recruitment scope is narrower.",
)

practices.title: Your turn: design the logging capture contract
practices.prompt: Choose how to capture logging information while preserving the phrase “where relevant”. A form consuming this model must be able to distinguish field presence from applicability.

fields.label: logging-mechanisms field
fields.correct_feedback: Optional presence supports capture without inventing universal requiredness. Missing information still needs interpretation.
fields.hint: A field shape describes presence; it does not determine whether a legal condition applies.

options.label: Always required
options.feedback: This invents a universal presence requirement from a conditional source statement.

options.label: Omit the field from the model
options.feedback: Omitting the field loses a useful capture target for relevant logging information.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

fields.label: Where the qualification belongs
fields.correct_feedback: A separate evidenced descriptive rule survives in the bundle. It does not execute the applicability decision.
fields.hint: The independent consumer must still be able to retrieve the qualification.

options.label: Only in notebook commentary
options.feedback: Notebook commentary is not part of the consumer bundle; the qualification would be lost.

options.label: Automatic compliance classifier
options.feedback: The descriptive rule is not an executable compliance classifier.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

practices.outcome: Your design combines an optional field with the instructions-logging-information rule. The consumer reads both; absence does not establish inapplicability.
practices.solution:
AttributeDefinition.string(display_name="Logging mechanisms")
# Keep the relevance condition in the evidenced
# instructions-logging-information RuleDefinition.

practices.title: Your turn: repair identity without erasing useful fields
practices.prompt: Two editions may share a document title and provision code. Choose the builder operation that removes that unsafe identity assumption, and what readable information to retain.

fields.label: Operation on provision-identity
fields.correct_feedback: remove_key() removes the uniqueness claim while retaining the concept and its attributes.
fields.hint: A key is a claim about identity; it is not the readable attribute itself.

options.label: remove_attribute()
options.feedback: Deleting a readable field does not specifically remove the unsafe uniqueness claim.

options.label: remove_concept()
options.feedback: Removing the whole concept would discard the provision meaning and its references.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

fields.label: Readable fields after the repair
fields.correct_feedback: Keep the document name and provision code; add the edition-aware locator as a structured field.
fields.hint: A value can remain useful even when it is unsuitable as a key.

options.label: Delete both fields
options.feedback: The fields remain useful for display and navigation; the key was the unsafe part.

fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

practices.outcome: The provision retains its identity and readable attributes. The unsafe key is removed and the locator records the edition context; no new uniqueness key is inferred.
practices.solution:
builder.remove_key(
    concept=provision,
    key=provision.get_key(name="provision-identity"),
)
# Keep both attributes; add the structured locator next.

practices.title: Your turn: find the two objects the consumer needs
practices.prompt: Use the refined model inspector above. Enter the lookup name of the optional logging attribute and the separate rule preserving its relevance condition. Enter names, not display labels or IDs.

fields.label: Attribute lookup name
fields.correct_feedback: This name resolves the optional string attribute; its generated ID is a separate identity.
fields.hint: Inspect instructions-for-use → attributes. Lookup names use lowercase words separated by hyphens.
fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

fields.label: Rule lookup name
fields.correct_feedback: This name resolves the evidenced descriptive qualification the consumer must retain.
fields.hint: Filter the model inventory for logging and inspect the definition whose kind is rule.
fields.fallback_feedback: Use the stable lookup name shown in the model inspector.

practices.outcome: You found the shape and the separate meaning that must travel with it. In C9 you will retrieve both from an independently loaded bundle.
